gr.satz.kettenregel.worum:
From the tower equation a rule for slopes follows immediately: one level higher, the curve is steeper by the factor “$\ln a$ times
function value there”. Because the function values grow rapidly, the slopes grow even more rapidly.
gr.satz.kettenregel.genau:
For every differentiable tetration $T$ to base $a$ and every $x>-2$:
$$T'(x+1)=\ln a\cdot T(x+1)\cdot T'(x).$$
gr.satz.kettenregel.warum:
Write the tower equation as $T(x+1)=a^{T(x)}=e^{T(x)\ln a}$ and differentiate with respect to $x$. The chain rule gives
$$T'(x+1)=e^{T(x)\ln a}\cdot\ln a\cdot T'(x)=T(x+1)\cdot\ln a\cdot T'(x).$$
gr.satz.kettenregel.einordnung:
All further differentiation rules of this strand follow from this: [[gr.kor.produktformel]], [[gr.satz.vorzeichen]],
[[gr.satz.zweite_ableitung]]. For fractional steps there is an extension with fractional products ([[kl.satz.bruchprodukt]]).

kn.gescheitert.regulaer_an_L.worum:
Below $\eta$ one builds the tetration at the real fixed point. Above $\eta$ only the complex pair $L,\bar L$ remains. The first thought:
just do the same construction at $L$. This does indeed give a solution of the equation — only it is
not real on the real axis. This failure shows what Kneser had to repair.
kn.gescheitert.regulaer_an_L.genau:
Let $b>\eta$, $L$ the fixed point of $b^z$ with $\operatorname{Im}L>0$ and $\lambda=L\ln b$ (one has $|\lambda|>1$). With the Poincaré function $\Psi$
($\Psi(\lambda w)=b^{\Psi(w)}$, $\Psi(0)=L$, $\Psi'(0)=1$) every $F(x)=\Psi(\lambda^xc)$ is a holomorphic superfunction of $b^z$. None of them is
real on the whole real axis. The choice of $L$ instead of $\bar L$ breaks the mirror symmetry $T(\bar z)=\overline{T(z)}$.
kn.gescheitert.regulaer_an_L.warum:
1. Equation: $F(x+1)=\Psi(\lambda\cdot\lambda^xc)=b^{\Psi(\lambda^xc)}=b^{F(x)}$.
2. Because $|\lambda|>1$, $\lambda^xc\to0$ for $x\to-\infty$, hence $F(x)\to\Psi(0)=L$. A real function cannot tend to a nonreal number.
3. Mirroring everything gives the same construction at $\bar L$. Both fixed points are on an equal footing; whoever selects one loses the symmetry.
4. Incidentally: $\Psi$ never takes the value $0$ (every value is $b^{\text{something}}$). A regular solution at $L$ with $F(0)=1$ would therefore have $F(-1)=2\pi ik/\ln b$
   with $k\ne0$ — it cannot hit the value $T(-1)=0$ of any genuine tetration at all.
kn.gescheitert.regulaer_an_L.beispiel:
Base $e$: $L=0.31813+1.33724\,i$, $\lambda=L$. If one normalizes so that $F(0)=2$, then $F(-1)=\ln2$ and $F(-2)=\ln\ln2=-0.3665$ — real. In between
not: $F(-\tfrac12)=1.0980+0.0972\,i$, whereas Kneser delivers $1.2329$ at the same height. One step further back comes $F(-3)=-1.0037+\pi i$,
after which the curve spirals into $L$.
kn.gescheitert.regulaer_an_L.einordnung:
Below $\eta$ exactly this construction works, because the fixed point is real ([[kl.satz.regulaer]]). Kneser corrects the defect with a
periodic function ([[kn.konstr.kneser]]); that every other solution differs from one by such a function is stated by [[fg.satz.allgemeine_loesung]].
